tank_description: An exceptionally armoured defender capable of withstanding almost anything frontally. The M1E1 excels at aggressive actions using both its abilities and its powerful main gun to make your enemies avoid whatever area you happen to choose.

strengths.title: Exceptional Protection
strengths.description: The M1E1 boasts formidable frontal armor, capable of withstanding the majority of direct fire. This exceptional protection makes it exceedingly challenging for opponents to dislodge it from a well-defended location.

strengths.title: Strong Firepower
strengths.description: The M1E1's strong and reliable main gun allows it to deal damage as effectively as it absorbs it, quickly punishing any enemies within range. Its minigun further enhances its damage output in combat giving the M1E1 surprising burst potential.

strengths.title: Easy to Learn
strengths.description: The M1E1's combination of traits results in a highly forgiving tank. Its simple-to-understand toolkit and strong defensive profile provide a safety net for new players as they familiarize themselves with the game.

strengths.title: Decent Mobility
strengths.description: Despite its size, the M1E1 is not sluggish. Its capable hull and turret traverse enable it to quickly react to threats and prevent enemies from outmaneuvering it, and whilst it's top speed is limited, it's gearing ensures that it can be maintained easily allowing it to keep up with engagements.

strengths.title: Jack of All Traits
strengths.description: While the term "jack of all trades" often implies "master of none," that doesn't apply to the M1E1. This tank allows players to experiment with nearly every playstyle and perform both offensive and defensive roles with competence. It may be the starter tank, but it is a viable tank at any level.

weaknesses.title: Poor at Range
weaknesses.description: With its poor gun ballistics, the M1E1 suffers from a very short effective range. Engaging targets beyond 80-100m results in a drastic drop in damage thus making it vulnerable to enemies who understand this limitation, especially marksmen.

weaknesses.title: Limited Build Variety
weaknesses.description: A significant drawback of the M1E1, though not on the battlefield, is its status as the "entry" tank. This results in a scarcity of viable build options, potentially diminishing its appeal for experienced players despite the power of its few common configurations.

weaknesses.title: Large Critical Zones
weaknesses.description: The M1E1's large engine, ammo racks and fuel tanks are prime targets. Consequently, even slight angling can expose these critical vulnerabilities, allowing prepared enemies to inflict significant damage. Drivers of the M1E1 must make an effort to present their best angles in all engagements.

weaknesses.title: Poor Side and Rear Armour
weaknesses.description: The M1E1's impressive frontal defenses are sharply contrasted by its weak side and rear armour. Presenting even a slight angle to the enemy can open you up to damaging shots, and auto-cannons will readily tear through its thinly protected flanks. Prioritizing a head-on engagement is paramount to mitigating these vulnerabilities.

weaknesses.title: Poor Rear Gun Arcs
weaknesses.description: The vehicle's large engine creates a significant obstruction, preventing it from effectively engaging threats behind it. This "hump" can and will be exploited by smaller vehicles and can be hard to counter. M1E1 players should therefore always be aware of whats behind them and have a plan deal with such situations.

tank_summary: The M1E1 in World of Tanks: HEAT is a powerful defender that excels as an aggressive anchor. Unlike the XM1V, it thrives in the thick of the action, directly shielding teammates and dictating the objective. Opponents rightly fear its aggressive presence, as the M1E1's combat style revolves around overwhelming firepower: striking hard, striking fast, and maintaining relentless pressure.

The M1E1's forgiving design and low barrier to entry make it highly accessible. Players will find its inherently strong characteristics and simple, direct toolkit easy to master, which is perfect for helping newcomers develop essential skills and understand core gameplay mechanics.

At its core, the M1E1 is a close-quarters brawler and should be played with this in mind. However, be careful not to overextend. even the M1E1 needs support. Focus on shielding your team, drawing enemy attention, and dictating the engagement.
